question_record.context: As part of a security incident that began with an email containing a malicious URL (`http://kn017721628.wittytree-b6f239d6.northeurope.azurecontainerapps.io/`) being delivered to the mailbox `santiago@vnevado.alpineskihouse.co` and subsequently removed, it was observed that a user sent phishing emails from within the organization possibly indicating their account had been compromised. Further investigation revealed that a process was injected with suspicious code potentially connecting to a C2 server or opening a listening port, which escalated until finally a malicious URL was clicked on a device.
question_record.question: What was the final malicious URL that was clicked on, indicating the continuation of the suspicious activities?
solution: The email account with SID `S-1-5-11-7842151660-4834030208-105586563-1139` received and later had an email with a malicious URL removed.
A user with AadUserId `a2d0f7c2-b0a0-43bd-bce0-27d8ae3be4d0` was observed to have sent phishing emails from their device.
A process on host `mb-winclient` was injected with potentially malicious code.
A malicious URL `https://ym018491661.wittytree-b6f239d6.northeurope.azurecontainerapps.io/` was clicked on that device.

41.name: A process was injected with potentially malicious code
41.description:
A process has injected code into another process, indicating suspicious code being run in the target process memory. Injection is often used to hide malicious code execution within a trusted process. 
As a result, the target process may exhibit abnormal behaviors such as opening a listening port or connecting to a command and control server.
